# Personal Details

Identity, experience narratives, technical profile, and career context. An agent
reads this first when generating resumes, cover letters, or interview prep.

Brain-dump here. Detail beats polish: the more specific the narratives and
numbers, the better the tailored output. This file is never sent to an employer.

---

## Who I Am
<Current title at current employer, since when, and what the role is. Then prior
roles in one line each with dates. Where you are based. Degree and school. Anything
distinctive: publications, leadership, community roles.>

State which title tailored resumes should use in the name heading. That is always
your actual current job title, never the title you are applying for.

## What I Work On
<The system or product you own, at what scale, built on what. Include real numbers:
nodes, requests per day, uptime, team size, dollars saved. Note explicitly what you
do NOT use, so an agent does not assume the standard stack.>

If this describes a former role, say so and note that it should be written in past
tense.

## Key Value Created
- **<Initiative> (<dates>):** <What changed because of you, with a number.>
- **<Platform scale>:** <The headline metrics you want appearing on resumes.>
- **<Other durable wins>**

## Key Narratives for Resume Tailoring
Detailed stories to draw from. Condense and adapt them; do not copy verbatim.

### <Narrative title> (<role>, <dates>)
<The situation, what you personally did, and the measurable outcome. Several
paragraphs is fine. Note which interview questions this story answers well.>

## Technical Identity
- **Primary languages:** <daily production languages first>
- **Infrastructure:** <...>
- **Data:** <...>
- **CI/CD:** <...>
- **Security:** <...>
- **Observability:** <...>
- **Databases:** <only what you have run in production>

## Professional Intersection
<The two or three domains you sit between. This is what makes you specific rather
than generic.>

## Hands-On Coding Identity
<How much production code you write, and how to phrase it. If you want resumes to
avoid manager-sounding framing, say so here with the exact language to prefer.>

## Leadership Style
<Team size, mentoring, code review, cross-functional coordination, interviewing.>

## Certifications
- **<Certification>** (<dates>): <what it covers and when it is worth surfacing>

## Honest Gaps and Depth Calibration
Where the resume lists something but the real depth is limited, or where target
roles commonly want something you have not built. Used for gap analyses and for
calibrating how confidently to present a skill. **This section is what keeps
generated resumes honest, so be blunt.**

- **<Technology>:** <What you have actually done with it versus what a posting
  will assume. How to frame it. What not to claim.>
